top_categories.workout_context: 105ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Race-pace efforts that mimic L'Étape Parma's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before race day.
At L'Étape Parma, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.

Road-specific control matters at L'Étape Parma. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 83 miles.
8,726ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of L'Étape Parma. Train it until it feels boring.
At mile 60 of 83, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
8,726ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at L'Étape Parma. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 8,726ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Low-cadence force work supports 8,726ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.

race_overlay.weather: Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks before L'Étape Parma. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for L'Étape Parma’s 83 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at L'Étape Parma. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at L'Étape Parma rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Race Simulation, and Over Under to prepare you for 83 miles of mixed terrain in Parma, Emilia-Romagna, Italy.
